chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Circumcise your children at seven days, for it is purer and faster for the growth of the flesh, and indeed the earth dislikes the urine of the uncircumcised.
And by this chain, it was said that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The piercing of the ear of the boy is from the Sunnah, and his circumcision at seven days is from the Sunnah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended age for circumcising boys in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the *Mustahabb* (recommended) time for circumcision at seven days, aligning with the Prophet's practice and emphasizing ritual purity (*taharah*) by removing the foreskin that traps impurities. The mention of the earth disliking the urine of the uncircumcised highlights the physical and spiritual cleanliness associated with this act, while the inclusion of ear piercing reflects the broader cultural and religious context of bodily adornment and tradition (*Sunnah*) in early Islamic society.
